testName: IISER IAT - Units, Dimensions & Dimensional Analysis Set 3 (20 Questions)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] The SI unit of luminous intensity is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The seven SI base quantities include luminous intensity with unit candela (cd).
Step 2: Lux is the unit of illuminance (derived), lumen is luminous flux (derived), watt is power (derived).
Step 3: Only candela is the base unit for luminous intensity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] Which of the following has the dimensions of [ML²T⁻²]?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Torque = Force × Distance = [MLT⁻²][L] = [ML²T⁻²].
Step 2: Pressure = [ML⁻¹T⁻²], Surface tension = [MT⁻²], Viscosity = [ML⁻¹T⁻¹].
Step 3: Note that torque and energy have same dimensions but different physical nature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] The least count of a screw gauge with pitch 0.5 mm and 50 circular scale divisions is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Least Count (LC) = Pitch / Number of circular scale divisions.
Step 2: LC = 0.5 mm / 50 = 0.01 mm.
Step 3: This means the screw gauge can measure up to 0.01 mm precision.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] Image-based: The screw gauge figure shows main scale reading 2 mm and circular scale reading 35 divisions. With pitch 0.5 mm and 50 circular divisions, what is the diameter?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Least Count = 0.5 mm / 50 = 0.01 mm.
Step 2: Main Scale Reading = 2 mm.
Step 3: Circular Scale Reading = 35 × 0.01 mm = 0.35 mm.
Step 4: Total Reading = 2 + 0.35 = 2.35 mm.
questions.imagePrompt: Technical diagram of a screw gauge (micrometer) showing: Main scale with 0-5 mm markings where the sleeve edge shows 2 mm clearly passed and 2.5 mm not yet reached, circular thimble scale with 0-50 divisions where the 35th division aligns with the reference line, labeled 'Screw Gauge Measurement' with clean white background, engineering drawing style with clear dimension lines

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] The dimensions of Planck's constant are:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: From E = hν, we get h = E/ν.
Step 2: [E] = [ML²T⁻²], [ν] = [T⁻¹].
Step 3: [h] = [ML²T⁻²]/[T⁻¹] = [ML²T⁻¹].
Step 4: Same as angular momentum, confirming quantization.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] If force F, length L, and time T are fundamental units, the dimensions of mass are:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Let [M] = [F]^a [L]^b [T]^c.
Step 2: [F] = [MLT⁻²], so [M] = [MLT⁻²]^a [L]^b [T]^c = [M^a L^(a+b) T^(-2a+c)].
Step 3: Equating: a=1, a+b=0 so b=-1, -2a+c=0 so c=2.
Step 4: [M] = [F¹L⁻¹T²].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] The percentage error in volume of a sphere is determined from radius measurement. If radius has 2% error, the volume error is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Volume V = (4/3)πr³, so V ∝ r³.
Step 2: Taking logarithm: ln(V) = ln(4π/3) + 3ln(r).
Step 3: Differentiating: ΔV/V = 3(Δr/r).
Step 4: Percentage error = 3 × 2% = 6%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] Image-based: The graph shows log(T) vs log(L) for a simple pendulum. If slope is 0.5 and intercept is 0.3, what is the period when L = 1 m?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Log-log plot: log(T) = m·log(L) + c, where m = slope = 0.5, c = intercept = 0.3.
Step 2: This means T = 10^0.3 × L^0.5 ≈ 2 × √L.
Step 3: When L = 1 m, T = 2 × √1 = 2.0 s.
Step 4: This matches T = 2π√(L/g) with appropriate constants.
questions.imagePrompt: Log-log graph paper showing log(T) on y-axis vs log(L) on x-axis, straight line with slope 0.5 marked with triangle rise/run, y-intercept at 0.3 when x=0, grid lines visible, labeled axes 'log(T)' and 'log(L)', scientific plotting style with data points scattered closely around the line

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] The dimensional formula of coefficient of viscosity η, from F = ηA(dv/dx), is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: From F = ηA(dv/dx), we get η = F/[A(dv/dx)].
Step 2: [F] = [MLT⁻²], [A] = [L²], [dv/dx] = [LT⁻¹/L] = [T⁻¹].
Step 3: [η] = [MLT⁻²]/([L²][T⁻¹]) = [MLT⁻²]/[L²T⁻¹] = [ML⁻¹T⁻¹].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] In a new system where unit of mass is 5 kg, unit of length is 20 m, and unit of time is 1 minute, the numerical value of 1 Newton in this system is:
questions.explanation: 1 N = 1 kg·m·s⁻². New base units: M₂ = 5 kg, L₂ = 20 m, T₂ = 60 s. Using dimensional conversion: n₂ = n₁ × (M₁/M₂)¹ × (L₁/L₂)¹ × (T₁/T₂)⁻² = 1 × (1/5) × (1/20) × (1/60)⁻² = (1/100) × 3600 = 36. Therefore 1 N = 36 new units of force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] The dimensional formula of magnetic flux is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Magnetic flux Φ = BA, and from Φ = LI (inductance × current).
Step 2: [L] = [ML²T⁻²A⁻²] (self-inductance).
Step 3: [Φ] = [ML²T⁻²A⁻²][A] = [ML²T⁻²A⁻¹].
Step 4: Alternatively from Faraday's law: ε = -dΦ/dt, so [Φ] = [ε][T] = [ML²T⁻³A⁻¹][T] = [ML²T⁻²A⁻¹].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] Image-based: The experimental setup shows a meter bridge for measuring resistance. If the balancing length is 40 cm from the left end for resistances R and S, what is the ratio R/S?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Meter bridge principle: R/S = l/(100-l), where l is balancing length from R side.
Step 2: Given l = 40 cm, so 100-l = 60 cm.
Step 3: R/S = 40/60 = 2/3.
Step 4: Therefore ratio R:S = 2:3.
questions.imagePrompt: Physics experimental diagram showing meter bridge (Wheatstone bridge) setup: Uniform resistance wire 100 cm long mounted on wooden board, galvanometer in middle with jockey contact, resistance R connected on left side (40 cm mark), resistance S on right side (60 cm mark), battery and key in series, labeled 'Meter Bridge Experiment' with length markings 0-100 cm, clean technical illustration style

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] The van der Waals constant 'b' in (P + a/V²)(V-b) = RT has dimensions of:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: By principle of homogeneity, b must have same dimensions as V.
Step 2: [V] = [L³] (volume).
Step 3: Therefore [b] = [L³].
Step 4: Constant 'a' has dimensions [ML⁵T⁻²] from a/V² having pressure dimensions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] The resistance R = V/I has percentage errors in V and I as 3% and 2% respectively. The percentage error in R is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: For R = V/I, taking logarithm: ln(R) = ln(V) - ln(I).
Step 2: Differentiating: ΔR/R = ΔV/V + ΔI/I (errors add for division).
Step 3: Percentage error = 3% + 2% = 5%.
Step 4: Note that even though it's V/I, both relative errors contribute positively to the total uncertainty.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] Which of the following is a dimensionally consistent equation?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Check (A): [v]=[LT⁻¹], [at²]=[LT⁻²][T²]=[L] - inconsistent.
Step 2: Check (B): [s]=[L], [at]=[LT⁻²][T]=[LT⁻¹] - inconsistent.
Step 3: Check (C): [v²]=[L²T⁻²], [u²]=[L²T⁻²], [as]=[LT⁻²][L]=[L²T⁻²] - consistent.
Step 4: Check (D): [s]=[L], [(u+v)/t]=[LT⁻¹/T]=[LT⁻²] - inconsistent.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] Image-based: The table shows repeated measurements of a physical quantity. What is the mean value and standard deviation?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Readings: 3.45, 3.40, 3.42, 3.38, 3.44.
Step 2: Mean = (3.45+3.40+3.42+3.38+3.44)/5 = 17.09/5 = 3.418 ≈ 3.42.
Step 3: Deviations: 0.032, -0.018, 0.002, -0.038, 0.022.
Step 4: Squared deviations: 0.001024, 0.000324, 0.000004, 0.001444, 0.000484. Sum = 0.00328.
Step 5: Standard deviation σ = √(0.00328/5) = √0.000656 ≈ 0.0256, or using n-1: √(0.00328/4) = √0.00082 ≈ 0.0286. Mean absolute deviation ≈ (0.032+0.018+0.002+0.038+0.022)/5 = 0.112/5 = 0.0224. Standard error or expanded uncertainty gives approximately ±0.12 when reported with 95% confidence or appropriate coverage factor.
questions.imagePrompt: Data table showing repeated measurements of a physical quantity: Column 1 'Trial' with values 1-5, Column 2 'Reading' with values 3.45, 3.40, 3.42, 3.38, 3.44, all in same units, table with horizontal lines and clear headers, scientific data recording format

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] The dimensional formula of impulse is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Impulse J = F × Δt = change in momentum.
Step 2: [F] = [MLT⁻²], [Δt] = [T].
Step 3: [J] = [MLT⁻²][T] = [MLT⁻¹].
Step 4: Same as momentum [mv] = [M][LT⁻¹] = [MLT⁻¹], confirming J = Δp.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Units and Measurements] Image-based: The figure shows a traveling microscope focused on a mark. The main scale reads 2.3 cm and the Vernier scale shows 6th division coinciding. If 1 MSD = 0.5 mm and 10 Vernier divisions = 9 MSD, what is the correct reading?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Least Count = 1 MSD - 1 VSD = 0.5 mm - 0.45 mm = 0.05 mm = 0.005 cm.
Step 2: Main Scale Reading = 2.3 cm.
Step 3: Vernier reading = 6 × 0.005 cm = 0.030 cm.
Step 4: Total reading = 2.3 + 0.030 = 2.33 cm.
Step 5: Note: Some may interpret main scale as 2.30 cm, giving 2.330 cm, but standard is 2.33 cm.
questions.imagePrompt: Technical diagram of traveling microscope scale: Main scale showing 2.3 cm mark clearly passed (with 2.0 and 2.5 cm markings visible), Vernier scale alongside with 10 divisions where the 6th division aligns with a main scale line, 1 MSD = 0.5 mm indicated, clean engineering drawing style with zoomed view of the coinciding division
